facts.text: Coupeville was laid out in the 1850s by Captain Thomas Coupe, after whom the town is named.
The town sits on Penn Cove, where the historic Coupeville Wharf stretches along the waterfront and hosts Washington’s longest‑running farmers market.
A self‑guided walking tour maps 65 historic sites, including the Island County Historical Museum that chronicles Indigenous peoples and early settlers.
Ebey’s Landing National Historical Reserve, established in 1978, protects the first and only National Historical Reserve in the nation and surrounds Coupeville.
In 1911, Lovejoy expanded ferry service from Coupeville, founding the Island Transportation Company that operated steamers to Port Townsend.
Coupeville’s climate is drier than much of western Washington, lying in the rain shadow of the Olympic Mountains.
